title: SCALPELLO-GDP: a frontier model edits the weights of Qwen3.5-0.8B directly. One Householder reflection of a 'repetitive re-checking' direction lifts held-out math accuracy from 9.4% to 53.6% (384 paired problems), with no training
read_level: full (English PDF of Zenodo record version 1.1, id 24422781, main text Secs 1-11; Appendix A problem list skimmed); code zip not opened
metadata_mismatch: 24416417 is the Zenodo concept id; the API resolves to version record 24422781 (v1.1). PDF title wording differs slightly ('9.38% to 53.65% (384 paired problems, 171 gains, 1 loss)'; '12 attention output projections'). Author matches.
why_wsp: gpt-6-astra, via API, writes Python in an offline no-gradient kernel holding Qwen3.5-0.8B weights and applies a closed-form Householder reflection of a 'repetitive re-checking' residual direction to 12 attention output projections, using 25 forward passes for feedback.
domain: LLM math reasoning (removing thinking loops; GSM8K/MATH train-split practice problems)
editor: gpt-6-astra (OpenAI Responses API, reasoning effort high)
interface: code/tensor tools (persistent Python kernel, no gradients, plus forward-pass tool)
loop: closed-loop with feedback (25 forward passes; 12 paired edit comparisons on 32 dev problems, then frozen)
self_editing: no; 'the editor itself is not modified'
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: 'relative change per tensor 6.6–9.2%; 25.2 M parameters.' (Sec 3.7); 12 tensors each 1024 x 2048

headline_results.quote: accuracy 9.38% → 53.65% (+44.27 ± 2.56 points, 95% bootstrap CI [39.32; 49.22]; exact McNemar p = 5.8 × 10−50 )
answers cut at the token limit 91.7% → 28.1%.
A random-direction reflection had no clear effect (+3.1±5.5 points).

headline_results.claim: Gains are from finishing within budget
headline_results.quote: Of the 171 gains, 170 were answers in which the original model reached the 8,192-token limit without writing any boxed answer

cost.quote: Editor cost: $8.43 for 92 calls (cap $60); GPU work was local.

cost.claim: Held-out pass wall time on T4
cost.quote: the held-out passes lasted 119–121 minutes each.

baselines_and_controls: Unedited model on same problems with shared seeds (paired); random-direction reflection control (same 12 tensors, s=2); alternative edit families and tensor subsets (Table 2).
runs_and_variance: 'One sample per problem, one run, one editor' (Sec 9); six held-out cohorts with paired SE, bootstrap CI, McNemar.
robustness_of_edits: Released checkpoint kept in bf16 and evaluated in fp16 on T4; no fine-tuning or longer-budget test; authors expect smaller gain at 32,768 tokens and possibly on larger Qwen3.5 models (untested).
verification: statistical: paired bootstrap, exact McNemar; static search of editor code for gradient/optimizer use; saved tensors recomputed to relative error 5e-8; network audit of every forward pass
memorization_vs_reasoning: Editor follows the exp8 prompt of Takehi et al. harness; the edit 'adds no mathematical knowledge: it reduces looped re-checking'. No test of editor reasoning vs recall.
limitations_stated: Not official benchmarks (train-split practice problems); 8,192 vs 32,768 token budget; one sample, one run, one editor; 32 dev problems; closed paid editor; network monitor polls every 0.5 s.
code_or_data: Zenodo scalpello_code_results_v1.0.zip; edited model https://huggingface.co/odelpa/qwen3.5-0.8b-scalpello-b2-gdp and Ollama ollamagdp/qwen3.5-0.8b-scalpello-b2-gdp
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi, Teoh, Zhang, Khattab 2026 Sparks of WSP (blog and MIT-licensed harness, exp8 prompt)
notes_for_survey: Independent low-budget replication of the Takehi et al. Qwen3.5-0.8B anti-loop result with half the forward budget and a quarter of the token cap; full edit history, random-direction control, and per-problem outcome list released. Gains are almost entirely due to answers finishing within the token cap.
